fact: Communications Minister Sam George said at the ACR2 opening that Ghana has a localisation policy under which local data and traffic processed on clouds outside the country will have to be hosted in Ghana; the document gives no instrument name or compliance date.

The bidding document states that NITA's two national data centres, in Accra and Kumasi, operational over the past 10 years, serve as central hubs for the Government of Ghana's IT operations and provide data storage, with about 90% of capacity used; the Accra core network backbones all government network services.

Graphic Online reports that the primary National Data Centre in Accra and a secondary centre at KNUST in Kumasi, managed by NITA with Alcatel-Lucent and Huawei Technologies Ghana, will host ministries', departments' and agencies' applications, initially email, antivirus and document management systems; the launch was held the day before the 2016-01-26 article, so 2016-01-25.

DatacenterDynamics reports that the government-opened NITA data center in Accra, with a secondary replica at KNUST in Kumasi, will provide Ghanaian government agencies with email, antivirus and document management systems; dated by the article's published date, as it gives no other date.
